platforms.title: A Clinical Study of Lashuna Kalpa & Rasnadi Taila Uttar Basti in Artava Kshaya w.s.r. to Hypomenorrhoea
platforms.subtitle: Postgraduate dissertation in Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
platforms.abstract: Artava Kshaya (hypomenorrhoea) is a common menstrual complaint in reproductive-age women and a frequent cause of fertility concern. This randomised clinical study was undertaken in the Department of Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga, Dr. N.R.S. Govt. Ayurvedic College, Vijayawada, to evaluate the efficacy of Lashuna Kalpa and Rasnadi Taila administered by Uttar Basti in the management of Artava Kshaya w.s.r. to Hypomenorrhoea. A sample of 30 subjects diagnosed with Artava Kshaya was recruited from the outpatient department of Prasuti Tantra and Stree Roga at Achanta Lakshmipathi Ayurvedic Hospital, Vijayawada. Diagnosis followed the classical vyadhi pratyatma lakshana — yathochita kala adarshanam (intermenstrual interval over 35 days), alpartava (reduced quantity of menstrual blood) and yoni vedana (lower abdominal pain) — in women aged 18–40 with scanty bleeding for two to three consecutive months, with anaemia, systemic illness, endocrine disorders and androgen-producing tumours excluded. Intervention combined oral Lashuna Kalpa churna (12 g twice daily with ksheera, ghrita or navaneet) with Rasnadi Taila administered by Uttar Basti. Each subject was assessed on an individual proforma covering history, physical signs and symptoms, dosha and dushya pareeksha, with the findings categorised and scored and analysed statistically. Lashuna Kalpa was prepared as a fine churna of shade-dried clove, and Rasnadi Taila was prepared from the classical kwatha and kalka dravyas — rasna, yashtimadhu, devadaru, malati, bala, chitraka, guduchi, kantakari and yuthika — boiled with jala, gomutra and godugdha in moorchita tila taila to madhyama paka. The findings support the use of Uttar Basti as a safe, low-cost, non-invasive and clinically effective intervention in Artava Kshaya, with significant improvement in the assessed clinical parameters.

platforms.title: Role of Uttarbasti in Yonivyapada
platforms.subtitle: AADHYA — Uttarbasti Session, with a supporting seminar presentation
platforms.abstract: Without Tridosha, no disease can form or manifest. Of the three, Kapha and Pitta are non-motile, while motility is attributed exclusively to Vata — and it therefore follows that vitiation of Kapha and Pitta most often requires an initiation from Vata Dosha. Basti has good therapeutic efficacy in normalising a vitiated Vata, which makes it a rational primary intervention in Yonivyapada, the umbrella term in Stri Roga covering almost all diseases of women. Uttarbasti carries both Shamana and Shodhana effects, and the drugs used in it are prepared in an oil base; depending on the condition, the formulation properties that act are Ushna, Tikshna, Vyavayi, sometimes Sheeta, Balya and Brimhana. The proposed mode of action is Srotoshuddhikara — the clearing of the srotas — together with stimulation of follicular cells and nourishment of the endometrium. Properly performed Uttarbasti produces desirable effects on several parameters of the female reproductive system.

platforms.title: The Role of Panchakarma in Vandhyatwa (Female Infertility): A Comprehensive Review
platforms.subtitle: Conference presentation — Sushruta Ayurvedic Research Forum, Pune
platforms.abstract: Vandhyatwa (female infertility) is one of the most common yet least discussed clinical presentations in Prasuti Tantra. This comprehensive review evaluates the role of Panchakarma in the management of female infertility, examining both Shodhana (purificatory) and Shamana (palliative) approaches as described in classical texts. The review covers the indications for Virechana, Vamana, Basti and Nasya in the context of reproductive disorders, together with the role of Ahara (diet), Vihara (lifestyle) and Dinacharya as the foundational substrate of any fertility protocol. The paper argues that Panchakarma works best not as an isolated procedure but as the preparatory and corrective stage that makes subsequent conception-oriented care effective, and it discusses the contemporary literature supporting these classical indications.

platforms.title: Delivery of Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR)
platforms.subtitle: Diagnosis, surveillance and the timing and mode of delivery in fetal growth restriction
platforms.abstract: Intrauterine growth restriction is one of the most consequential complications of pregnancy, associated with elevated perinatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impact. This seminar covers the aetiology and classification of fetal growth restriction, the antenatal surveillance methods including biophysical profile, amniotic fluid assessment, Doppler studies and the role of lung maturation, the significance of the L:S ratio and phosphatidylglycerol, and the timing and mode of delivery in the growth-restricted fetus. It also presents the Ayurvedic understanding of garbhapata and the adjunctive management of the maternal side, while emphasising the multidisciplinary surveillance required for these high-risk pregnancies.

platforms.title: The Conceptual Approach of Preconceptional Care in Ayurveda
platforms.subtitle: Structured abstract with Introduction, Materials & Methods, Results and Discussion
platforms.abstract: Preconceptional care in Ayurveda emphasises a holistic approach to ensuring optimal health before conception. Nature has given the human body the great responsibility of pregnancy, and in the present era, where lifestyle-related issues and environmental factors affect fertility, couples seeking a "Supraja" — a healthy, physically, mentally and intellectually strong child — are drawn to Ayurvedic principles. A comprehensive review of Ayurvedic texts and contemporary studies was conducted, covering dietary recommendations, lifestyle modification and herbal interventions aimed at enhancing fertility, supplemented by practitioner survey and case-study insight. The findings indicate that Rutukal, Dinacharya, Rutucharya, Yogabhyasa, Panchakarma, Pranayama, Ahara-Vihara, Achar Rasayana, counselling, meditation, Garbhini Paricharya and targeted herbal interventions collectively contribute to enhanced fertility and improved overall health in both partners. The discussion underscores a sustainable path to conception that ensures parents are physically and mentally prepared before the journey ahead, and identifies the need for further research to quantify these benefits and integrate Ayurvedic principles with modern reproductive health practice.

platforms.title: Ayurveda for Public Health
platforms.subtitle: Swasthavritta, Dinacharya, Ritucharya, Rasayana and community medicine
platforms.abstract: Ayurveda is an ancient medical science of human civilisation and a holistic health science that addresses the individual as well as the community. Owing to severe pollution, climate change, population growth and other socio-economic pressures, the world today faces a strong survival strain on all living beings and on nature; maintaining the wholeness of nature and human health is a pressing obligation that cannot be ignored. Ayurveda has distinctive advantages here, because it directly fulfils social health demands. Swasthavritta — the promotion of health — is among the strongest and most unique aspects of Ayurvedic medicine. Ayurveda places emphasis on rules of conduct and their effect on the social and behavioural aspects of life, addressing both preventive and curative dimensions of health and promoting wellbeing through organised community effort. Classical Ayurvedic texts already describe infectious disease, immunity and nutrition within their own idioms. With Dinacharya, Ritucharya, Rasayana and Vajikarana, individual health can be improved; and with Yoga, meditation and immune-modulating Ahara, the wider public-health aim can be met.

platforms.title: Vomiting in Pregnancy: Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy in Ayurveda
platforms.subtitle: Management of Garbhini Chardi and its classical formulations
platforms.abstract: Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy is one of the earliest and most universal symptoms of gestation, described in the classical texts as Garbhini Chardi. This seminar presents the Ayurvedic understanding of vomiting in pregnancy, the doshic basis of the condition, the classical diagnostic and therapeutic approach, the role of Ahara-Vihara and the specific formulations indicated in pregnancy with their indications, precautions and rationales, and the differentiation from the pathological vomiting of later pregnancy such as hyperemesis gravidarum. The presentation also addresses the limits of classical management and the point at which modern intervention is required, aiming to give the postgraduate audience a safe and practical synthesis.

platforms.title: Sadarasa in Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
platforms.subtitle: The classical principle of mental balance in the clinical management of women's disorders
platforms.abstract: Sadarasa — equipoise of mind — occupies a distinctive place in Ayurvedic theory, which holds that the mental component of disease is not an adjunct but a parallel axis of treatment. This seminar examines the concept of Sadarasa in relation to Prasuti Tantra and Stree Roga, exploring classical definitions of manas, the relationship between manas and sharira, the mechanisms by which psychological disturbance is described as a cause or an aggravating factor in disorders of menstruation, conception, pregnancy and the puerperium, and the classical therapeutic methods — including Sattvavajaya, Achara Rasayana and manas-antara treatment — used to restore balance. The presentation connects this framework to the modern clinical reality of stress-related menstrual and fertility complaints.

platforms.title: Role of Dinacharya for Immunity
platforms.subtitle: A seminar on the classical daily regimen as the basis of immune health
platforms.abstract: Dinacharya is defined as the daily routine. According to Ayurveda, one should follow Dinacharya in order to lead a healthy and disease-free life. Ayurveda gives more emphasis on the prevention of disease than on its treatment, and Dinacharya is the practical vehicle for that principle: it establishes balance in one's constitution, regularises the biological clock, aids digestion, absorption and assimilation, and generates self-esteem, discipline, peace, happiness and longevity. This seminar presents Dinacharya as the daily immune strategy — a structured, timed sequence of Ahara, Vihara and Achara that keeps the doshas in balance and maintains the body's natural defence capacity, and contrasts it with modern behaviour-based approaches to immune resilience.

platforms.title: Prasava Vigyana — Ayurvedic Obstetrics
platforms.subtitle: Management of normal labour: the classical four stages and their monitoring
platforms.abstract: Prasava Vigyana is the classical science of management of labour. This seminar presents the Ayurvedic framework for the conduct of normal labour, working through the four stages of prajasma with their characteristic signs, the assessment of the onset of labour and the progress of the uterine contractions, the ahara-vihara and positional management advised in each stage, the use of the classical formulations indicated for each stage, and the management of the third stage including the prevention of postpartum haemorrhage and the care of the newborn. The classical model is set alongside contemporary evidence-based practice and partograph-based monitoring.

platforms.title: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
platforms.subtitle: Diagnosis, complications and the Ayurvedic management of madhumeha in pregnancy
platforms.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus is now the commonest medical complication of pregnancy and carries substantial maternal and fetal consequences, including macrosomia, hypertensive disorders and neonatal hypoglycaemia. This seminar covers the screening and diagnostic criteria, the glucose targets and monitoring required, the nutritional and lifestyle management of the condition, the pharmacological options, the intrapartum and postpartum management, and the long-term risk of progression to type 2 diabetes. Alongside the modern pathway, the presentation discusses the Ayurvedic understanding of madhumeha in pregnancy — the doshic basis, the classical ahara-vihara prescription and the role of herbo-mineral formulations — and evaluates where classical and contemporary management can be integrated responsibly.

platforms.title: Epilepsy in Pregnancy
platforms.subtitle: Seizure management through pregnancy, labour and the puerperium
platforms.abstract: Epilepsy in pregnancy presents a dual therapeutic challenge: controlling seizures while avoiding harm to the fetus through medication, and managing the labour itself. This seminar reviews the epidemiology and classification of seizure disorders in pregnancy, the effect of pregnancy on seizure control, the principles of anti-epileptic drug management in the antenatal, intrapartum and postpartum periods including the teratogenic considerations, the management of eclampsia and status epilepticus, and the Ayurvedic understanding of the condition and its adjuvant role. The talk is aimed at equipping the postgraduate with a decision framework for a high-risk obstetric patient.

platforms.title: Effect of Pumsavana Karma in Conception
platforms.subtitle: A classical review of the first of the Shodasha Samskaras for Garbhasthireekarana
platforms.abstract: Pumsavana Karma, the first of the Shodasha Samskaras, is performed to secure a healthy, intelligent and prosperous progeny — the classical aim of Suputrakameeya. The karma may be performed immediately prior to conception (Pushyanakshatra) and is directed at Garbhadharana (conception) and Garbhasthireekarana (the settling of the embryo). The 10th–16th day of the menstrual cycle is identified as the optimal window for conception, and Pushya Nakshatra — one of the fourteen Purusha Nakshatras and among the most auspicious for medicinal preparations and therapeutic administration — is the prescribed time for its performance. This article reviews the principles and practice of Pumsavana Karma, examining its rationale, timing, procedure and therapeutic intent, and presents it as a safe, cost-effective and evidence-informed approach to improving conception outcomes. The review positions Pumsavana as a bridge between classical Samskara doctrine and contemporary fertility-seeking practice.

platforms.title: Concepts of Rasa in Relation to Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
platforms.subtitle: Six rasa, their therapeutics, and the classical prohibition on rasa in pregnancy
platforms.abstract: Rasa occupies a distinctive position in Ayurvedic pharmacology as the most refined and most potent preparation class, formed through shodhana, marana and bhavana processes. This seminar explores the concept of Rasa in relation to Prasuti Tantra and Stree Roga, tracing the classical definitions of rasa, the pharmacological action attributed to rasaushadhi, the relationship between rasa and agni, and the classical cautions governing their use across the reproductive life-cycle — particularly in pregnancy, where specific rasa preparations are contraindicated. The discussion also addresses the modern pharmacological framework of drug action and how rasaushadhi effects may be correlated with known therapeutic and adverse-reaction profiles, providing a grounded basis for their cautious clinical application.

platforms.title: Concept of Pathya in Relation to Prasuti Tantra & Stree Roga
platforms.subtitle: Diet, regimen and the therapeutic principle of pathya in women's health
platforms.abstract: In Vachaspata, the verse reads "pathya-pathe, marge, hite chikitsad-au, hitakarakabhoktryadravyabhedahe" — pathya is that which walks the path of benefit and is wholesome in ahi (food), vihara (conduct) and chikitsa (treatment). The word pathya derives from the root path, literally a way or channel. In Shabdakalpadrum, pathya is described as that which is beneficial to the patient, while apathya harms. Because the characteristics and properties of food change according to season, place and person, pathya must change accordingly. In the Yogaratnakara, the three most important factors in treating disease are etiology, drug treatment and pathya. Judicious planning of treatment by proper understanding of pathya therefore yields a far more effective eradication of disease than medicine alone. This seminar applies the principle of pathya specifically to Prasuti Tantra and Stree Roga, where dietary and behavioural regulation carries unusual weight across conception, pregnancy, labour and the puerperium.

platforms.title: Complications of the Stages of Labour
platforms.subtitle: Dystocia, haemorrhage and the management of abnormal progress in labour
platforms.abstract: This seminar covers the complications that may arise at each of the three stages of labour — the first, second and third — and their management in the Ayurvedic obstetric framework. It addresses abnormal progress and the recognition of obstructed and prolonged labour, the management of postpartum haemorrhage and the third-stage complications of retained placenta and uterine atony, and the indications for referral. Presenting the classical approach to prasava-vyapad, the talk also builds the practical decision-making sequence a postgraduate must follow when a labour deviates from the expected course.

platforms.title: Artava Kshaya (Oligohypomenorrhoea)
platforms.subtitle: Aetiology, diagnosis and management of scanty menstruation
platforms.abstract: Artava Kshaya — scanty menstruation — is among the most under-reported complaints in Stree Roga, yet it is frequently the earliest signal of a fertility concern and is often dismissed by patients and clinicians alike. This seminar covers the classical definition and classification of Artava Kshaya, the doshic aetiology with particular reference to Vata and the role of Ama, the differential diagnosis from physiological variation and from other menstrual disorders including amenorrhoea, the investigation approach, and the therapeutic management combining ahara-vihara, aushadhi and specialised procedures such as Uttar Basti. The presentation also addresses the long-term consequences of untreated Artava Kshaya on reproductive health.

platforms.title: Applied Anatomy of the Abdomen
platforms.subtitle: Regional anatomy oriented to abdominal examination and surgical practice
platforms.abstract: Applied anatomy is anatomy with a purpose: it teaches the relationships that determine what the surgeon sees, what the obstetrician palpates and what the radiologist images. This seminar covers the regional anatomy of the abdomen as it is actually used in practice — the quadrants, the surface markings of the viscera, the planes and fascial layers that determine surgical access, the anatomy of the abdominal wall and its inguinal canal, the retroperitoneum, and the vascular and neural relations of the abdominal viscera — presented specifically for the obstetric and gynaecological clinician, with clinical correlations drawn from examination, imaging and operative practice.

platforms.title: Abnormal Development of the Fallopian Tube and Ovary
platforms.subtitle: Embryology, Müllerian anomalies and their fertility implications
platforms.abstract: Congenital anomalies of the fallopian tube and ovary are a significant and under-recognised cause of subfertility and recurrent pregnancy loss. This seminar traces the normal embryological development of the Müllerian and gonadal systems and the critical windows in which developmental errors occur, then classifies the congenital anomalies of the fallopian tube — including agenesia, hypoplasia, accessory tubes and tubal diverticula — and of the ovary, relating each to its effect on ovulation, tubal patency and fertility potential. The presentation concludes with the clinical implications, the imaging and operative evaluation, and the referral and management pathways for these patients.

platforms.title: Role of Dinacharya in the Prevention of Health Hazards of Pollution
platforms.subtitle: A supervised compilation in the Department of Swasthavritta
platforms.abstract: This supervised compilation examines the role of Dinacharya — the classical daily regimen — in preventing the health hazards posed by pollution, in the Department of Swasthavritta, Parul Institute of Ayurveda, Parul University. The work surveys the classical framework of Ahara (diet), Vihara (behaviour) and their rules of combination, place, time, quantity and quality, and then maps each of the major contemporary pollution categories — air, water, soil, noise, light, thermal and radioactive — against the specific protective and remedial measures that Dinacharya prescribes. Because classical texts address pollution-related illness as an accumulation of doshas disturbed by specific etiological factors, the compilation argues that preventive daily routine is a more realistic first line of defence than any downstream treatment, particularly in communities where environmental exposure cannot be immediately controlled. The work concludes that a structured, seasonally appropriate daily routine remains a clinically meaningful and accessible intervention for pollution-related morbidity.
